subject: Reasoning
description: Covers complex pointer relations and family tree logic.

questions.stem: Pointing to a woman in a picture, a man says, 'She is the mother-in-law of the wife of the father of my only son.' How is the woman related to the man?

options.option_text: Mother
Wife
Daughter
Sister

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Let's break this down from the end backward:
1. "my only son" -> The man's son.
2. "the father of my only son" -> The man himself.
3. "the wife of the father of my only son" -> The man's wife.
4. "She is the mother-in-law of [the man's wife]" -> The mother-in-law of a man's wife is the man's own mother.
Therefore, the woman in the picture is the man's mother.
DECOY BUSTING: If the prompt said "mother-in-law of my wife", it's obvious. The phrase "father of my only son" is just a long-winded decoy way of saying "me".
EXAM INSIGHT: The key to these "pointing to a picture" puzzles is replacing long phrases with the direct relationship, step-by-step.

questions.stem: A, B, C, D, E, and F are members of a family. B is the son of C but C is not the mother of B. A and C are a married couple. E is the brother of C. D is the daughter of A. F is the brother of B. Who is the mother of B?

options.option_text: A
C
D
E

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Let's build the family tree:
1. "B is the son of C but C is not the mother of B." -> If C is a parent but not the mother, C MUST be the FATHER.
2. "A and C are a married couple." -> Since C is the father (male), A must be the wife (female). Therefore, A is the mother.
3. "E is the brother of C" -> E is the uncle.
4. "D is the daughter of A" -> D is B's sister.
5. "F is the brother of B" -> F is B's brother.
The question asks: Who is the mother of B? The answer is A.
DECOY BUSTING: The trick is "C is not the mother". Many students get confused here, forgetting that a parent can be a father.
EXAM INSIGHT: Always look out for "Parent but not mother/father" tricks. It simply determines the gender of the parent.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, Deepak says, 'His father is the only son of my grandfather.' How is the person in the photograph related to Deepak?

options.option_text: Uncle (father's or mother's brother by birth)
Brother (has the same father as Deepak)
Son (child born to Deepak and his spouse)
Nephew (son of one of Deepak's siblings)

questions.explanation: Deepak's grandfather's only son = Deepak's father. The person's father is therefore Deepak's father, making the person Deepak's brother. Nephew is the classic wrong pick — that would require the person to be a child of Deepak's sibling, not a sibling of Deepak himself.

questions.stem: Meena is the sister of Rohan. Sunita is the mother of Rohan. Prakash is the husband of Sunita. How is Meena related to Prakash?

options.option_text: Sister (shares Sunita as a common mother)
Niece (daughter of Prakash's own sibling)
Daughter (child born to Prakash and Sunita)
Wife (Meena is wed to Prakash in the same family)

questions.explanation: Prakash is Sunita's husband → Prakash is Rohan's father. Meena is Rohan's sister, so they share the same parents → Meena is also Prakash's daughter. Niece is wrong because that would require Meena to be a child of Prakash's sibling, not Prakash himself.

questions.stem: In a family, P is the father of Q. Q is the sister of R. S is the wife of P. T is the son of R. How is T related to S?

options.option_text: Grandmother (S is the mother of T's parent R)
Mother (S is T's own biological mother)
Great-grandmother (two generations above T)
Aunt (S is the sister of T's father or mother)

questions.explanation: S is wife of P → S is mother of Q and R. T is son of R → R is T's mother. Therefore S (R's mother) is T's maternal grandmother. Great-grandmother is the tempting wrong answer — it would need three generational steps, but S→R→T is only two, making S the grandmother, not great-grandmother.

questions.stem: Rahul says, 'Deepa's father is the only male child of my paternal grandmother.' How is Deepa related to Rahul?

options.option_text: Niece (daughter of Rahul's brother or sister)
Cousin (daughter of Rahul's paternal uncle)
Sister (shares the same father as Rahul)
Daughter (Rahul is Deepa's biological father)

questions.explanation: Rahul's paternal grandmother's only male child = Rahul's father. Deepa's father is that same person → Deepa and Rahul share the same father → Deepa is Rahul's sister. Cousin is the classic error — that would require Deepa's father to be Rahul's uncle, but 'only male child' locks him as Rahul's father.

questions.stem: A woman says about a man, 'His mother is the only daughter of my father-in-law.' How is the man related to the woman?

options.option_text: Brother-in-law (husband's own male sibling)
Son (the woman's own biological child)
Nephew (son of the woman's husband's sibling)
Cousin (related through a common grandparent)

questions.explanation: Father-in-law = woman's husband's father. His only daughter = woman's husband's sister. Man's mother = husband's sister → man is son of husband's sister → man is the husband's nephew and, by extension, the woman's nephew. Son is the tempting wrong choice — the man's mother is the husband's sibling, not the woman herself, so the woman is not his mother.

questions.stem: A man says to a woman, 'Your only brother's son is my wife's brother.' How is the woman related to the man's wife?

options.option_text: Sister-in-law (married to the man's wife's sibling)
Maternal aunt (the wife's mother's own sister)
Paternal aunt (the wife's father's own sister)
Mother (the woman is the one who gave birth to the wife)

questions.explanation: Let B = woman's only brother. B's son is man's wife's brother → man's wife and B's son are siblings → man's wife is also B's child (his daughter). The woman is B's sister → the woman is the paternal aunt (father's sister) of the man's wife. Maternal aunt is the most tempting wrong answer, but the relation flows through B who is the wife's father, making it the paternal side, not maternal.

questions.stem: In a family: (i) J is the brother of K. (ii) L is the daughter of M. (iii) M is the father-in-law of J. (iv) N is the son of K. (v) K is female. How is N related to L?

options.option_text: Paternal aunt (father's sister or father's kin)
Maternal aunt (wife of N's maternal uncle J)
Sister (born to the same parents as N is)
Cousin (child of N's own parent's sibling)

questions.explanation: K is female; J is K's brother → J is male. M is J's father-in-law → J married M's daughter = L. K is N's mother and J's sister → J is N's maternal uncle. Since J is married to L, L is the wife of N's maternal uncle = N's maternal aunt. Cousin is the tempting wrong answer, but L belongs to the parent's generation (one level above N), not the same generation. Paternal aunt would be N's father's sister; here the connection runs through N's mother K, placing it firmly on the maternal side.
